gold_answer: The three works address the limitations of a plain MLP decoder for continuous super-resolution in distinct ways. Jiang et al. (HIIF) introduce a hierarchical positional encoding that operates on local sampling points at multiple scales, allowing the implicit function to capture fine structural details without relying solely on deeper or wider MLPs. The Shenzhen/Sun Yat-sen team (LMF) instead restructures the computation: they keep decoding in a shared latent space at the low-resolution, high-dimensional level using an MLP, and only perform lightweight, independent rendering in the high-resolution, low-dimensional space, which avoids the quadratic cost of decoding directly in HR high-dimensional space and thus makes high-frequency rendering more practical. Lee and Jin (LTE) take a frequency-domain route, adding a local texture estimator that predicts dominant frequencies of image patches in 2D Fourier space, enabling the implicit function to explicitly model high-frequency texture components that a standalone MLP would otherwise miss. In short, HIIF enriches the input encoding hierarchically, LMF reshapes where and how the heavy decoding happens to make detail generation efficient, and LTE injects an explicit Fourier-based texture prior to recover high-frequency content.

answer:
LMF and Meta-SR both address arbitrary-scale super-resolution with a single model, but they use different mechanisms.

Meta-SR handles arbitrary scale factors through a meta-upscale architecture. Its network contains a Feature Learning Module that extracts low-resolution features and a Meta-Upscale Module that replaces the conventional fixed upscale module（来源：Meta-SR: A Magnification-Arbitrary Network for Super-Resolution, p.3）. For an arbitrary scale factor, the Meta-Upscale Module dynamically predicts the weights of upscaling filters from the scale factor and coordinate information, and these predicted filters are applied to the feature maps to generate a high-resolution image of arbitrary size（来源：Meta-SR: A Magnification-Arbitrary Network for Super-Resolution, p.1; p.4）. The module includes location projection, weight prediction, and feature mapping（来源：Meta-SR: A Magnification-Arbitrary Network for Super-Resolution, p.4）. Because the filter weights are generated by a prediction network rather than stored separately for each scale, Meta-SR can use one model for arbitrary, including non-integer, scale factors and can continuously zoom the same image with multiple scales（来源：Meta-SR: A Magnification-Arbitrary Network for Super-Resolution, p.1; p.2; p.8）.

LMF instead formulates arbitrary-scale super-resolution as latent-modulated continuous image rendering. It decouples the high-resolution high-dimensional decoding process into shared latent decoding in the LR high-dimensional space and independent rendering in the HR low-dimensional space（来源：Latent Modulated Function for Computational Optimal Continuous Image Representation, p.1）. Given an encoder latent code, an HD latent MLP generates latent modulations, which then adjust a lightweight LD render MLP to predict high-resolution pixel values（来源：Latent Modulated Function for Computational Optimal Continuous Image Representation, p.2）. LMF moves time-consuming operations and large MLPs into latent space, leaving a minimal render MLP for rendering; it also separates feature unfolding, used only by the latent MLP, from local ensemble, used only by the render MLP（来源：Latent Modulated Function for Computational Optimal Continuous Image Representation, p.4）. In contrast, Latent Modulated Function (LMF) addresses computational inefficiency by decoupling the super-resolution process into two stages: a shared latent decoding in low-resolution high-dimensional space using an MLP, followed by independent rendering in high-resolution low-dimensional space, which reduces the quadratic computational cost typically associated with high-resolution high-dimensional decoding. While Meta-SR focuses on unifying arbitrary scale factors into one model, LMF optimizes the computational paradigm of continuous image representation to make arbitrary-scale super-resolution more practical.

DiffuFNO_SR and SRNO both address arbitrary-scale super-resolution, but they emphasize different mechanisms: DiffuFNO_SR combines Fourier-spectral operator learning with diffusion refinement, while SRNO formulates super-resolution as continuous operator learning with attention-based latent-basis updates.

DiffuFNO_SR uses a diffusion framework built around a Weighted Fourier Neural Operator, WFNO（文献：DiffuFNO_SR.pdf，p.8）. Its high-frequency strategy is explicitly spectral: Mode Rebalancing in WFNO emphasizes critical frequency components and high-frequency details（文献：DiffuFNO_SR.pdf，p.8；文献：DiffuFNO_SR.pdf，p.1）. The reconstruction is then further refined by a diffusion process, which iteratively recovers intricate textures and high-frequency components by modeling the conditional distribution of high-resolution images given low-resolution inputs（文献：DiffuFNO_SR.pdf，p.2；文献：DiffuFNO_SR.pdf，p.8）. This design is motivated by the limitation that standard FNOs or MLPs may underrepresent high-frequency information because of mode truncation or spectral bias（文献：DiffuFNO_SR.pdf，p.2）.

SRNO, by contrast, treats low-resolution and high-resolution image pairs as continuous functions approximated with different grid sizes and learns a mapping between the corresponding function spaces（文献：SRNO.pdf，p.1）. It first lifts low-resolution pixel values into a higher-dimensional latent feature space using a CNN-based encoder（文献：SRNO.pdf，p.3；文献：SRNO.pdf，p.8）. For high-frequency recovery, SRNO relies on a multilayer operator-learning architecture that explores a common latent basis and then refines an instance-specific basis through Galerkin-type attention; this dynamic latent-basis update is described as crucial for “hallucinating” high-frequency information from the low-resolution input（文献：SRNO.pdf，p.2）.

For global structure, DiffuFNO_SR exploits the resolution invariance and global-dependency modeling ability of neural operators（文献：DiffuFNO_SR.pdf，p.5）. It uses Fourier/spectral convolution to capture global patterns and long-range dependencies, and it further combines WFNO’s spectral features with spatial features from an Attention-based Neural Operator through a Gated Fusion Mechanism, which adjusts the influence of global and local features（文献：DiffuFNO_SR.pdf，p.2；文献：DiffuFNO_SR.pdf，p.3；文献：DiffuFNO_SR.pdf，p.8）.

SRNO captures global structure mainly through operator learning and Galerkin-type attention over continuous function representations, with the paper emphasizing the importance of capturing global correlations for super-resolution（文献：SRNO.pdf，p.2）. Its continuous function-space formulation also allows arbitrary-scale, discretization-independent super-resolution（文献：SRNO.pdf，p.2；文献：SRNO.pdf，p.8）, and SRNO is reported to be strong in capturing global image structures（文献：SRNO.pdf，p.8）.

In short, DiffuFNO_SR’s strategy is frequency-spectral plus diffusion-based: it reweights Fourier modes to strengthen high-frequency reconstruction and uses diffusion refinement to improve texture detail（文献：DiffuFNO_SR.pdf，p.1；文献：DiffuFNO_SR.pdf，p.8）. SRNO’s strategy is continuous-mapping plus attention-based: it learns arbitrary-scale super-resolution as a function-space transformation and uses Galerkin-type attention and dynamic latent bases to recover details and global structure（文献：SRNO.pdf，p.1；文献：SRNO.pdf，p.2）.
gold_answer: DiffuFNO_SR employs a Weighted Fourier Neural Operator (WFNO) with Mode Re-balancing to emphasize critical frequency components, enhancing the reconstruction of fine-grained, high-frequency details. It also integrates a Gated Fusion Mechanism (GFM) that combines spectral features from WFNO with spatial features from an Attention-based Neural Operator (AttnNO), enabling the model to simultaneously capture both global structures and local details. In contrast, SRNO relies on a kernel integral mechanism implemented via Galerkin-type attention, which operates non-locally in the spatial domain to approximate continuous image functions across arbitrary grid sizes, focusing on grid-free continuum representation rather than explicitly emphasizing high-frequency components. While SRNO's multilayer attention architecture allows iterative refinement of the implicit image function, DiffuFNO_SR introduces a diffusion-based refinement process and an Adaptive Time-Step ODE solver to accelerate inference while maintaining output quality.

LINF generates high-resolution textures by treating arbitrary-scale super-resolution as conditional modeling of **local texture-patch distributions**. It was proposed to overcome prior arbitrary-scale methods that ignore the ill-posed nature of SR and rely on per-pixel L1 loss, which tends to produce blurry results（来源：Local Implicit Normalizing Flow for Arbitrary-Scale Image Super-Resolution，p. 1）. Specifically, LINF formulates SR as learning the distributions of local texture patches, using a coordinate-conditional normalizing flow together with a local implicit module that provides conditioning signals（来源：Local Implicit Normalizing Flow for Arbitrary-Scale Image Super-Resolution，p. 8）. The flow models a conditional patch distribution \(p(m_{i,j}\mid I_{LR}, x_{i,j}, s)\) and learns a bijective mapping between this local texture distribution and a latent Gaussian distribution（来源：Local Implicit Normalizing Flow for Arbitrary-Scale Image Super-Resolution，p. 3）. Super-resolution is then performed by generating local textures separately for each non-overlapping high-resolution patch, producing rich and reasonable details instead of over-smoothed outputs（来源：Local Implicit Normalizing Flow for Arbitrary-Scale Image Super-Resolution，p. 2）. Thus, LINF’s strategy is fundamentally a **local, distribution-based generative process over patches**, rather than an explicit image-wide continuous field model（来源：Local Implicit Normalizing Flow for Arbitrary-Scale Image Super-Resolution，p. 2; p. 8）.

GaussianSR, by contrast, establishes spatial dependencies by representing the image as a **continuous Gaussian field**. It models each pixel as a self-adaptive continuous Gaussian field rather than a discrete point value（来源：GaussianSR: High Fidelity 2D Gaussian Splatting for Arbitrary-Scale Image Super-Resolution，p. 2）. In its pipeline, discrete feature points are converted into Gaussian fields by assigning Gaussian kernels to pixels, and the feature at any arbitrary query position is computed from overlapping Gaussian functions whose influence is modulated by spatial location（来源：GaussianSR: High Fidelity 2D Gaussian Splatting for Arbitrary-Scale Image Super-Resolution，p. 3）. Because these Gaussian fields are rendered as mutually stacked fields, dependencies across spatial positions—including long-range dependencies—are established（来源：GaussianSR: High Fidelity 2D Gaussian Splatting for Arbitrary-Scale Image Super-Resolution，p. 1）. This continuous field can explicitly yield values at arbitrary query positions, which naturally supports arbitrary-scale upsampling（来源：GaussianSR: High Fidelity 2D Gaussian Splatting for Arbitrary-Scale Image Super-Resolution，p. 2; p. 7）.
gold_answer: LINF employs normalizing flows to explicitly model the probability distribution of texture details at varying scaling factors, enabling photorealistic synthesis by capturing the underlying data distribution. In contrast, GaussianSR abandons discrete pixel representations entirely, instead modeling each pixel as a continuous 2D Gaussian field whose stacked rendering establishes long-range spatial dependencies that enhance the representational capacity beyond what discrete latent codes can achieve.
